"Nudify" AI is banned in the EU from 2 December A new EU AI Act prohibition targets AI systems that generate non-consensual intimate images or child sexual abuse material, with fines up to 7% of global turnover. It reaches Indian AI companies with EU users. How does it compare with India's rules? New Article 5 ban AI labelling India vs EU Adv. Ashwani Kumar · Advocate | Data Privacy & Technology Law 01 / 08

Two deadlines, one date 1 · NEW PROHIBITED PRACTICE (ARTICLE 5) AI that generates CSAM or non-consensual intimate content Banned where that's the intended purpose ("nudifier" apps), and also where it's a reasonably foreseeable, reproducible outcome and the provider lacks adequate safeguards. 2 · ARTICLE 50(2) GRACE PERIOD ENDS Machine-readable marking of AI output Generative AI already on the EU market before 2 August 2026 must now mark its output. Newer systems had no grace period. 7% 3% or €35 million: maximum fine for or €15 million: maximum fine for prohibited practices transparency breaches Adv. Ashwani Kumar 02 / 08

WHO IS CAUGHT Not just nudify apps 1 Providers anywhere. The AI Act applies to providers placing systems on the EU market, and where a system's output is used in the EU, wherever the company is based. 2 General image and video tools. The "foreseeable outcome" limb reaches any generator that can produce such content without adequate safeguards. 3 Deployers too, where they use a system intentionally for that purpose. The change comes from the "Digital Omnibus" on AI, published in the EU's Official Journal on 24 July 2026. The same package delayed the high-risk rules to December 2027 and August 2028, but not this ban. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 03 / 08

Stop the harm at the source 1 Takedowns come too late. Once an intimate deepfake spreads, removal can't undo the harm. A duty on the tool that makes it matters. 2 A safeguards duty for generators. India's coming AI consultation paper should require image and video tools to block non-consensual intimate content of real people. 3 Foreseeable misuse. Make providers answerable when they ignore misuse they could have prevented. 4 One marking standard. Align India's labels and metadata with EU marking, so Indian companies don't build twice. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 06 / 08

WITH EU USERS Four weeks to 2 December Map your capabilities Can your model or app generate images or video of real people? Test for misuse Red-team for intimate and CSAM outputs; add prompt and output filters. Remove risky features "Undress" or face-swap features on real people without consent. Mark your output Visible labels plus machine-readable marking work for both India and the EU. Paper it Usage policies, abuse reporting, customer contracts with use limits, and records of your safeguards. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 07 / 08

TA K E AWAY The EU now regulates the tool, not just the content. India's rules act after a deepfake is made and shared. The EU's ban acts before. As India drafts its own AI law, protecting victims of intimate deepfakes should start with the systems that create them. Adv.
